parsed.explanation: The dominant structural facts are severe: a passed bill awaiting near-certain assent criminalising identifying as trans (up to 3 years), crossdressing, 'promotion', plus a duty-to-report that would actively engineer outing; an existing 'unnatural carnation knowledge' statute; documented mob justice; raids that shut the only community infrastructure; no legal recognition, anti-discrimination protection or shelter. Thin-data extrapolation from these signals resolves toward high risk, not midpoint. Mitigating: no enforcement record for the trans-specific offence yet, visitor application unresolved, and detailed violence documentation is dated (2017–18). No documented organised sweeps or custody-placement regime yet. This sits between the 0.25 anchors (organised coercion operating) and the pre-enforcement severity of the framework: latent identity criminalisation with a reporting lever, documented societal violence, and no recourse — high risk, at the lower edge of the band.
